unit_label: BRBL::MOD_APPENDIX::U01: Locate guarantee questions without confusing separate contract relationships

payload.title: Name the relationship and the event
payload.core_explanation_md:
A guarantee problem can involve creditor against surety, surety against principal debtor, or contribution between co-sureties. Start by identifying which relationship is in dispute. Then locate the relevant liability, continuing-guarantee, discharge, security or recourse provision. The fact one surety pays does not make every later claim the same cause of action.

A variation, release, forbearance, revocation or impairment of security can engage different rules. Keep the agreement, consent, transaction dates and amounts available while reading the full text. The appendix section route is a memory aid; the substantive contract unit supplies the independently authored explanation and application work.

self_check.prompt_text: Is co-surety contribution the same relationship as creditor recovery?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Identify the parties and the right being enforced.

payload.stem_md: A surety has paid and seeks reimbursement from the principal debtor. Which issue should the researcher distinguish from the original creditor claim?

options.text_md: The surety recourse against the principal debtor
options.explanation_md: Payment gives rise to a different relationship for analysis.
That does not identify the recourse right.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Payment gives rise to a different relationship for analysis.

payload.stem_md: A guarantee is challenged after a contract change. Why read the specific variation/discharge provision instead of only the liability heading?

options.text_md: The event may engage a separate qualified discharge rule
options.explanation_md: Liability and subsequent discharge require separate analysis.

options.text_md: The index automatically rewrites the guarantee

payload.correct_explanation_md: Liability and subsequent discharge require separate analysis.
